source_read: PMC HTML, PMC4823436 (BMJ Open publisher version, open access; not an author manuscript), read in full in the app's browser with get_page_text (abstract, strengths-and-limitations box, introduction, methods, results, discussion, footnotes, reference list), plus Figure 1 (flow diagram with per-outcome study counts) viewed on its PMC figure page. Online supplements 1-4 (search terms, quality scores, study-characteristics table, forest plots 1-8) not read; where a figure could only come from them it is said. Text saved in scratchpad/can-a/s219/gunn_2016_pmc_text.txt.

claims.overstatement: No overstatement of the source: the claim says 'is associated with' and states the authors' own caveat on tobacco and alcohol, which is more cautious than the review's abstract (cannabis use may increase adverse outcomes) and Discussion 3rd paragraph (exposure leads to low birth weight). Three small precision points, none changing a number: (1) 'pooled estimates are crude' is the editors' inference; the review states no adjustment (exact), and the mean differences are certainly unadjusted because they were pooled from group means and SDs, but for the odds ratios the review says only that ORs were taken from the papers or computed from their data, without saying whether any OR taken from a paper was adjusted (the forest plots that would show this are in online supplement 4, not read). (2) 'Preterm birth before 37 weeks': the review says 7 of the 8 PTB studies used the WHO <37-week definition (Methods), while the Results and Figure 1 count 9 PTB studies, so the definition was not uniform. (3) 'Tobacco and alcohol, which themselves cause low birth weight and early birth': the source names tobacco and heavy alcohol use (and also small for gestational age). The Apgar, birth-defect and perinatal-death results are narrative vote counts from 2 to 6 studies, not pooled estimates; 'showed no clear difference' is fair wording for that.
claims.note: Every number from this source re-found: 109.42 g (38.72 to 180.12; rounds to 109, 39 to 180), 10 studies, 4 lower, I2 63%; LBW OR 1.77 (1.04 to 3.01), 7 studies, 2 positive, I2 89%; NICU/ICU OR 2.02 (1.27 to 3.21), 4 studies, 3 positive, I2 78%; PTB OR 1.29 (0.80 to 2.08), 9 studies, I2 85%; gestational age -0.20 (-0.62 to 0.22), 5 studies, fixed effect; length -0.10 (-0.65 to 0.45), I2 59%; head circumference -0.31 (-0.74 to 0.13), I2 97%; anaemia OR 1.36 (1.10 to 1.69), 6 studies, fixed effect. The '6 studies' for length and for head circumference come from Figure 1 (the text says 9 studies reported length and 10 measured head circumference). Editors' count '15 of the 24 articles before 2000' recomputed from the reference list (included refs 13, 16-22, 24-39): before 2000 = refs 13, 20, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38 = 15; 2000 to 2014 = refs 16, 17, 18, 19, 21, 26, 29, 30, 39 = 9; same result. Range 1982 (Greenland) to 2014 (Bonello) confirmed. 'No absolute risks reported' holds for the main text; whether the forest plots in supplement 4 show event counts cannot be judged here. The editors' observation on NICU admission is correct: Discussion 4th paragraph discusses only cost and calls for attention, not whether admission reflects hospital practice toward babies of mothers known to use drugs. The parts citing Hall & Degenhardt 2009, Hall 2015 and Page 2020 are not from this source and were not checked.

anchors.locator: Results › Description of studies, 1st paragraph; Figure 1; reference list (refs 13, 16-22, 24-39)
anchors.extracted: Search to 1 April 2014; 6854 records, 881 full texts screened, 860 excluded, 3 added by hand search and author contact: 24 articles representing 19 unique studies. Designs: 1 cross-sectional, 1 case-control, 22 cohort; no randomized trials. Countries (article counts): USA 10, Canada 5, Australia 3, Netherlands 2, Iran, Jamaica, Spain, Brazil 1 each. Included articles published 1982 (Greenland) to 2014 (Bonello); reader's count: 15 of the 24 before 2000.

anchors.locator: Methods › Inclusion/exclusion criteria › Type of studies, 1st paragraph; Study population, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Only studies reporting outcomes of prenatal cannabis use while excluding other illicit drugs (eg cocaine, methadone) were included; because few studies accounted for tobacco and alcohol, studies with concurrent tobacco smoking and alcohol use were included. English-language publications only. Infant outcomes up to 6 weeks after birth.

anchors.locator: Methods › Data extraction, 1st paragraph; Methods › Data analysis, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Reviewers extracted each study's methods for handling confounding, but pooling used ORs with 95% CIs or SEs taken from the papers or computed from their data and, for continuous outcomes, group means and SDs (RevMan 5.3); fixed effect when heterogeneity acceptable, otherwise random effects. No adjusted pooled estimate and no adjustment of any kind is stated; whether any extracted OR was itself adjusted is not said.

anchors.locator: Results › Effects of prenatal use of cannabis on neonatal outcomes › Weight at birth, 1st paragraph; Abstract › Results; Figure 1 (Birth weight n=10)
anchors.extracted: Birth weight as a continuous outcome in 10 studies, 4 showing lower weight with exposure and 6 null; random effects: 109.42 g lower in exposed infants (95% CI 38.72 to 180.12; I2 63%). The abstract prints the pooled mean difference as a positive 109.42 g although it is a reduction.

anchors.locator: Results › Effects of prenatal use of cannabis on neonatal outcomes › Weight at birth, 1st paragraph; Figure 1 (Low birth weight n=7)
anchors.extracted: Low birth weight in 7 studies (the citation string also lists ref 15, a UNICEF report, not a study), 2 showing higher odds and 5 null; random effects pooled OR 1.77 (95% CI 1.04 to 3.01; I2 89%). LBW assumed to be <2500 g in all studies (Methods › Dichotomous variables).

anchors.locator: Results › Effects of prenatal use of cannabis on neonatal outcomes › Other maternal and child health outcomes, 1st paragraph; Figure 1 (NICU/ICU n=4; Gestational age n=5)
anchors.extracted: NICU or ICU placement in 4 studies (refs 16-18 positive, ref 24 null); random effects pooled OR 2.02 (95% CI 1.27 to 3.21; I2 78%). Gestational age in 5 studies (4 null, 1 lower); fixed effect pooled mean difference -0.20 weeks (-0.62 to 0.22). No association, by narrative count, with perinatal mortality (2 studies), anomaly (4 studies), days in hospital and several other outcomes.

anchors.locator: Results › Effects of prenatal use of cannabis on neonatal outcomes › Growth parameters, 1st paragraph; Figure 1 (Neonatal length n=6; Head circumference n=6; Preterm birth n=9)
anchors.extracted: Length reported in 9 studies, 6 pooled: mean difference -0.10 cm (-0.65 to 0.45; I2 59%). Head circumference measured in 10 studies, 6 pooled: -0.31 cm (-0.74 to 0.13; I2 97%). Preterm birth in 9 studies (3 higher odds, 6 null; ref 19 is cited in both groups and ref 28 in neither); random effects pooled OR 1.29 (0.80 to 2.08; I2 85%).

anchors.locator: Methods › Maternal and fetal outcomes included in meta-analyses › Dichotomous variables, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Preterm birth was classified by the WHO <37-week definition in 7 of the 8 included PTB studies (the Results and Figure 1 count 9). Only one study stated the WHO anaemia definition (haemoglobin <11 g/dL); the reviewers assumed all used it. NICU and ICU stays were combined into one outcome.

anchors.locator: Results › Effects of prenatal use of cannabis on neonatal outcomes › Neonatal assessments, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: No association with 1- and 5-minute Apgar scores (6 studies cited; narrative, not pooled). Single studies reported neurobehavioural differences (Brazelton scale, Prechtl assessment).

anchors.locator: Results › Effect of prenatal use of cannabis on maternal health outcomes, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 2nd paragraph; Figure 1 (Maternal anemia n=6)
anchors.extracted: Anaemia in 6 studies: 1 (Witter 1990) found higher odds, 5 null; fixed effect pooled OR 1.36 (95% CI 1.10 to 1.69). The positive study had 8350 participants, the largest sample in the review, and carried the greatest weight; the authors advise caution in interpreting the result.

anchors.locator: Discussion, 6th paragraph; Strengths and limitations box, 3rd bullet
anchors.extracted: Most studies did not exclude women who also used tobacco or alcohol, so a cannabis-only effect could not be determined; tobacco and heavy alcohol use are established causes of low birth weight, preterm birth and small for gestational age, so it is unknown whether the effects found come from cannabis or from alcohol and tobacco.

anchors.locator: Discussion, 7th and 8th paragraphs; Abstract › Conclusions and relevance
anchors.extracted: Self-reported use may have under-counted use; few studies defined anaemia, PTB or LBW. The authors conclude both that the effects of cannabis on maternal and fetal outcomes are still largely unknown (Discussion, 8th paragraph) and, in the abstract, that use 'may increase adverse outcomes for women and their neonates'; Discussion 3rd paragraph says exposure results in low birth weight.

key_findings.note: All Figure 1 counts re-read on the figure page; database counts sum to 4976 and 4976 + 1878 = 6854; exclusion reasons sum to 4065 (same as the card); 881 - 860 + 3 = 24.
Reader's own count from the reference list also gives 15 of 24 before 2000 (1982 to 2014).
Locator checked against the page's heading tree: 'Other maternal and child health outcomes' is an H4 under 'Effects of prenatal use of cannabis on neonatal outcomes', as the card gives it.

The parenthesis 'under 37 weeks' holds for 7 of the 8 PTB studies according to Methods › Maternal and fetal outcomes included in meta-analyses › Dichotomous variables (reporting issue 2 records the 8-versus-9 discrepancy).

key_findings.correction: The source names tobacco and HEAVY alcohol use as established causes of low birth weight, preterm birth and small for gestational age (Discussion, 6th paragraph); the finding's 'tobacco and alcohol, which are established causes' drops 'heavy'. Suggested wording: '... or to tobacco and alcohol use (tobacco and heavy alcohol use being, the authors say, established causes of low birth weight, preterm birth and small-for-gestational-age births)'. The same word is missing from the claim cl_can_pregnancy_birth.

reporting_issues.note: Refs 31 to 35 all have Fried as first author.
Found independently in step 1; ref 15 is the source cited for the <2500 g definition in Methods › Dichotomous variables.

Review side confirmed; the comparison with the protocol's wording was not checked (the protocol is a separate article, outside the pages this reader may open). Nuance: Methods › Assessment of heterogeneity says I2 was calculated only when the Q-test p was at or below 0.10, which explains a missing I2 for a fixed-effect pool with p above 0.10 but not for one chosen under the p at or below 0.10, I2 at or below 50% branch; the reader still cannot tell which branch applied.

Review side confirmed (no sensitivity analysis by risk of bias, no meta-regression, subgroup analysis said to be impossible, no reasons for full-text exclusions, the attempted restriction to women aged 18 or over in Discussion, 7th paragraph). The protocol side (PMC4360840) was not checked by this reader: separate article, outside the permitted pages.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 critically low is secure: items 11 (raw means and SDs pooled, no statement that any OR was adjusted) and 15 (publication bias not assessed) are critical flaws on the main text alone, and item 7 (860 full-text exclusions without list or reasons) is a third. Items 2 and 9 as partial yes are defensible; the protocol-dependent parts of item 2 were not checked by this reader.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: the abstract's 'may increase adverse outcomes' and Discussion 3rd paragraph's causal wording on low birth weight sit against the authors' own statement that a cannabis-only effect could not be separated from tobacco and alcohol; the abstract leads with anaemia, which the Discussion says rests on one study; the 'high quality' verdict is unsupported in the main text.

missed: Figure 1 also gives the number of distinct studies across the odds-ratio pools (12) and across the mean-difference pools (10); not on the card (minor).
Methods › Assessment of heterogeneity: I2 was calculated only for Q-test p at or below 0.10, which bears on reporting issue 5 (see note there).

For the claim editor: the claim cl_can_pregnancy_birth calls the pooled estimates 'crude', which is firmer than the card's own, accurate wording (the paper does not say whether any pooled OR was adjusted; the mean differences are unadjusted by construction). 'No adjustment stated' is exact; 'crude' is certain only for the four mean-difference pools.
